scope: One bounded official-GitHub provider-history leaf: test whether current public non-mutating repository/name/redirect/restore surfaces, plus opportunistic event history, can recover a prior repository incarnation after logical-name reuse when the predecessor repository ID is not retained. No O, other-worker, downstream, legacy, mutation, hosted compute or paid/finite-quota semantic input was used.

official_sources.observed_claim: GitHub redirects old repository locations after rename, but creating a new repository under the original name causes redirects to stop working.
GitHub redirects the previous location after transfer, but creating a new repository or fork at the previous location permanently deletes those redirects.
Some deleted repositories can be restored only within 90 days; restoration is therefore not a permanent predecessor-history witness.

The ordinary Get a repository route is keyed by current owner/repo and may return 301 for a move or 404 when no current resource/redirect is available; current same-name lookup is not predecessor-history by itself.

event_surface_treatment.claim_scope: This leaf does not rely on a guaranteed event-retention duration. It tests both transition-visible and unavailable/truncated/no-event states because a complete stateless incarnation witness must survive the latter. Opportunistic event visibility is evidence only when present; absence cannot prove no predecessor existed.
event_surface_treatment.acceptance_rule: A provider-history route must remain sufficient when the relevant predecessor transition is not discoverable from the current event window.

required_negative_cases: event retention/history truncation or no-event period
private/deleted predecessor represented by provider-unresolvable predecessor state
rename or transfer followed by logical-name reuse that destroys the redirect
API rate-limit/interruption with checkpoint rather than unsafe inference

observations: When a predecessor ID is retained, that retained identity can be used as a disambiguating input if a provider lookup for that identity remains available; this is conditional and does not solve lost-ID reconstruction.

When the predecessor ID is lost, a current owner/name lookup returns the current incarnation or a current redirect; it cannot by itself distinguish a same-name replacement from the historical predecessor.
Rename and transfer redirects are explicitly defeasible by logical-name reuse, so redirect continuity is not a permanent incarnation witness.
Deleted-repository restoration is bounded to a documented 90-day window, so it cannot provide an indefinite predecessor witness after retention expiry.

Event history can be opportunistically useful when a transition record is visible, but a complete mechanism cannot depend on it because the required negative includes unavailable/truncated/no-event history.
On API rate-limit/interruption the only safe action is fail-closed checkpoint/retry on a later invocation; transport unavailability supplies no authority evidence.

steps: Repository incarnation R1 exists at owner/name; its provider ID is not retained by the recurring Chat state.
R1 is renamed or transferred, initially creating an old-location redirect.
A new repository R2 is later created at the old owner/name, which GitHub documents as removing or overriding the redirect.
The relevant transition is absent from the currently discoverable event history, and R1 has been deleted beyond the documented restoration window.
A stateless invocation observes only current owner/name metadata for R2.
falsifying_trace.result: The listed public non-mutating surfaces contain no sufficient predecessor identity from which the invocation can prove that R1 existed or derive a monotonic incarnation lower bound. R2 is observationally compatible with a world in which it was the only repository ever at that logical name.
falsifying_trace.unsafe_if_accepted: Treating current same-name metadata, a missing event, or redirect failure as proof of predecessor retirement would allow ABA/logical-name-reuse confusion.

result.minimal_unresolved_child: A zero-cost, non-mutating provider-side predecessor/incarnation witness that remains discoverable after rename/transfer name reuse and predecessor deletion/restore expiry even when the caller retained no predecessor ID and no relevant event is available.
result.scope_guard: Applies only to the documented/current GitHub repository-name redirect, transfer, deletion-restoration and ordinary repository lookup surfaces tested here plus the explicit absent-event negative. It does not claim that undocumented/internal/future provider metadata cannot exist.

zero_dependency_zero_quota_assessment.repository_api_rate_limit_handling: Fail closed and resume from durable checkpoint on a later invocation; rate-limit capacity is transport, not compute or authority.
